ns2:section.sectionText: Advanced Fisheries Ecology is a graduate-level discussion course covering complex issues confronting fish conservation and fisheries management. The goals of the course are to (1) become informed on complex issues confronting fish conservation and fisheries management, (2) understand the science underpinning these issues and the various approaches used to address them, and (3) become confident in analyzing, assessing, and discussing different perspectives on contentious issues in applied ecology. PREREQUISITE: NRES 409 or an equivalent course in fisheries science from another institution.
